steps.what: Inspect defective equipment and capture observed facts
Enter defect facts into the report form
Verify and file the defective equipment report

tasks.design: Configure a reusable defect form in {OPS_SYSTEM}, testing existing maintenance forms first. The collector supplies observations, checks the completed report and files it; urgent hazard communication remains a separate task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated identifiers and form layout require manual entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms can reuse selected equipment identifiers and validate required fields.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising a fault and describing its safety implications need direct observation.
tasks.human_edge: The collector distinguishes observed symptoms from an unconfirmed diagnosis.
tasks.altitude: Less form entry; maintenance and safety authority stay unchanged.

reach.learn: Describe symptoms and equipment identity precisely

evidence.claim: Reusable maintenance forms can reduce repeated entry; these task savings are an unmeasured scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is collecting facts and filing one defect report, excluding repair and urgent dispatcher contact.

Collector produces equipment ID, observation time, location, symptom description and immediate action in s1; its 45 hours include capture. Missing identifiers or unclear symptoms are entered manually; no inferred defect code is required.
Test native forms before custom work; existing storage runtime earns no saving.
unknowns: Current report format and repeated entry time
research_questions: Does reuse of identifiers reduce total entry time without weakening defect descriptions?

incremental.description: Resolve form exceptions and maintain equipment selections

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B100, R85, gross15 minus3 upkeep gives net12. Low assumes only6 hours of entry reduction and the same upkeep; observation and final filing remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Communicate delays and safety problems to dispatchers

steps.what: Assess delays, unsafe sites, accidents or breakdowns
Communicate incident facts and coordinate a safe response with dispatchers

tasks.design: Keep assessment and live communication in person and through {TELEPHONY}. Existing communications equipment supports the exchange; a generated incident summary does not replace clarification or immediate safety coordination.
tasks.previous_blocker: Incidents are situational and may demand immediate questions.
tasks.enabler_now: No additional automation is justified within this task boundary.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete observations and changing road or site conditions.
tasks.human_edge: The collector explains uncertainty and responds to dispatcher questions.
tasks.altitude: No change in time or decision rights.

evidence.claim: Live incident coordination remains human work in this scenario.

assumptions: Boundary covers collector assessment and communication, excluding dispatcher labour, repairs and separate written defect reports.
Collector produces location, observed event and immediate risk during s1; capture is included in35 hours. Unknown facts are explicitly reported as unknown.
Existing telephony is already in use; no new system or upkeep is introduced, justifying zero incremental work.
research_questions: Is any material repeated entry outside the live exchange present?

incremental.description: No change to tools or process

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 and zero upkeep; no change to situational assessment or conversation is proposed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check road and weather effects on routes

steps.what: Find current road and weather information for the assigned route
Check local conditions and determine how the route is affected

tasks.design: Configure bookmarks in {OTHER}, the existing road and weather information service, for the assigned service area. The collector still checks notice relevance, observes local conditions and determines route effects.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the same local information pages can take repeated navigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing services can retain area selections and source bookmarks.
tasks.still_hard: A road notice does not establish access for a particular collection vehicle.
tasks.human_edge: The collector recognises local access constraints and unsafe conditions.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less navigation; routing authority stays unchanged.

reach.task: Assess vehicle access on affected roads
reach.learn: Vehicle clearance and local restriction interpretation

evidence.claim: Saved area selections can reduce navigation but do not determine collection-route safety.

assumptions: Boundary is checking route effects, not issuing a replacement route.

Dispatcher supplies the existing assigned route and service area through unchanged route planning. Collector selects and checks the area and notice freshness in s1; its15 remaining hours include that work. No structured closure feed is assumed; unavailable pages mean manual lookup.
Test native bookmarks first; no model interpretation or automatic route update is proposed.
unknowns: Available local information services and saved views
research_questions: Do saved views remain current and relevant across the collection area?

already_counted.description: Check area selection and notice relevance

incremental.description: Maintain source bookmarks and handle changed pages

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B100 R90, gross10 minus2 upkeep gives net8. Low assumes only2 hours navigation saved; physical observation and route judgement retain75 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Tag containers to inform customers of problems

steps.what: Inspect containers for excess garbage or prohibited items
Choose the appropriate existing tag and mark the observed problem
Attach the problem tag to the correct garbage or recycling container

tasks.design: Keep physical inspection, selection of existing printed tags and attachment manual. {DOCS} remains the source of collection rules; existing printed choices already simplify the notice.
tasks.previous_blocker: The collector must observe the actual contents and identify the correct container.
tasks.enabler_now: No new enabling technology changes those physical actions in this scenario.
tasks.still_hard: Mixed contents and ambiguous collection rules.
tasks.human_edge: The collector applies rules to what is actually visible and gives an accurate notice.
tasks.altitude: No change in work or authority.

evidence.claim: Printed tags assist notice selection but do not remove inspection or attachment work.

assumptions: Boundary ends when the tag is attached; customer remediation and collection-policy design are outside it.
Collector produces the observed problem in s1 and marks the matching tag in s2, with all capture time counted. Ambiguous cases use the existing manual escalation procedure.
Existing printed tags and rules remain unchanged; there is no added upkeep and their existing convenience earns no new saving.
research_questions: Are the existing tags clear enough for frequent container problems?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100, zero upkeep. Existing tags are the baseline; inspection and physical attachment are retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Small reductions in report entry and information navigation; physical collection and safety judgement remain central.
reach: Work with maintenance inspectors on useful defect descriptions
Work with recycling coordinators on clear container notices
role.ambitious_version: A collector who supplies reliable operational observations while retaining responsibility for safe field decisions.
